articles.title: George Kittle, Nick Bosa Injury Updates Given by John Lynch, Latest on 49ers Stars' Status vs. Rams
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle will travel with the team to Australia for its opener against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10, general manager John Lynch confirmed to Tim Kawakami of The San Francisco Standard.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle will travel with the team to Australia for its opener against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10, general manager John Lynch confirmed to Tim Kawakami of The San Francisco Standard.

Lynch also told Kawakami that Nick Bosa will travel with the team and both players are expected to play in the season opener.

Kittle suffered a torn Achilles in San Francisco's NFC Wild Card Round win over the Philadelphia Eagles. After undergoing surgery, he suggested to reporters he could suit up again "well before November."

The 32-year-old is on pace to comfortably hit that timeline.

San Francisco overhauled its receiving corps this offseason. The team signed Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel and also used a second-round pick on De'Zhaun Stribling. That turnover is compounded by the fact Ricky Pearsall already suffered a season-ending knee injury.

Kittle remains a dependable target when healthy. He had 57 receptions for 628 yards and seven touchdowns in his 11 appearances in 2025.

The rapport he has established with quarterback Brock Purdy is even more important, too, given how many new pieces the Niners added.

Having Kittle available for the opener would be a big luxury for the offense.

As for Bosa, he is recovering form an ACL tear that limited him to three game last season. The return of the former Defensive Player of the Year will be huge for San Francisco's defense and should help the team begin the season on a high note.

articles.title: Ryan Poles explains where Bears QB Caleb Williams has grown most
articles.summary: Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles discussed how head coach Ben Johnson has helped quarterback Caleb Williams get the joy back in his game.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have an opportunity to build off their success last year, reaching the NFC Divisional playoff round, sparked in a major way by the growth and play of quarterback Caleb Williams.

In his second season in the NFL, Williams had a brand new system led by head coach Ben Johnson, which saw the quarterback set a franchise record for most passing yards in a single season while leading a top-10 offense, but there's still plenty of room to grow.

On Tuesday, general manager Ryan Poles spoke about the trajectory of Williams' career as heads into Year 3 in the NFL, believing that the connection he's built with his head coach is key to long-term success.

Chicago Bears 53-man roster for 2026 season

"I think you see that joy back in his game where he's playing free," Poles said about the growth in his young quarterback. "I think he sees and identifies where he comes up short faster than what he did before, and I think that's where him and Ben (Johnson) are continuing to work really well together, trying to get better every single day."

There's no question that at least in the first year of their relationship, the Bears are getting what they had hoped for in the head coach-quarterback relationship, and now they'll look to build off of that first year success. If Williams can continue to make leaps in his game and development, not only will he be a highly-successful quarterback in the NFL, but he'll be the franchise cornerstone that the Bears have needed for decades.

articles.title: 11 days till Arizona Cardinals' opener: Remembering the 2011 season
articles.summary: With 11 days until the Arizona Cardinals' 2026 opener, let's look back at their 2011 season.
articles.body:
We continue the countdown to the start of the Arizona Cardinals ' regular season. Today, Wednesday, September 2, is 11 days away from the Arizona Cardinals' regular-season opener on Sept. 13 on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers.

With 11 days until Week 1, let's look back at the 2011 season for the Cardinals.

A look back at the 2011 season for the Cardinals

In 2011, we had to endure the NFL lockout. During the offseason, the Cardinals, reeling from Kurt Warner's decision to retire after 2009 and having suffered a 5-12 2010 season, they traded for quarterback Kevin Kolb in exchange for cornerback Domonique Rodgers-Cromartie and a second-round pick.

Kolb struggled with injuries. He suffered turf toe and had a concussion, only starting nine games. After a 1-6 start, they won five of their final six games to finish 8-8. Second-year quarterback John Skelton went 5-2 as a starter, and that triggered a QB competition for the following offseason.

Rookie cornerback Patrick Peterson, the fifth overall pick in the draft, returned four punts for touchdowns.

Peterson was a first-team All-Pro, too. Fitzgerald made the second team.

Kolb had the most passing yards with 1,955, nine touchdowns and eight interceptions. Skelton passed for 1,913 yards and 11 touchdowns, but he threw 14 picks.

Running back Beanie Wells had 1,047 rushing yards to lead the team. Fitzgerald had 80 catches for 1,411 yards and eight touchdowns.

Calais Campbell led the Cardinals with eight sacks. Richard Marshall's three interceptions on defense led the team, and five players had at least 10 pass breakups, led by Wilson's 14.

articles.title: Patriots' Clever Visual Illusion During Opponent Field Goals Spotlighted in Trending Photos
articles.summary: During the Bill Belichick era, the New England Patriots capitalized on whatever on-field edge they could find. In one such case, the team may have called upon the services of the scoreboard operator.
articles.body:
During the Bill Belichick era, the New England Patriots capitalized on whatever on-field edge they could find. In one such case, the team may have called upon the services of the scoreboard operator.

Ryan Paganetti, who worked for multiple NFL on the analytics and research side, discovered the Patriots would show the uprights on the video screen at Gillette Stadium when opposing kickers were lining up for field goals. That would create a difficult visual for kickers as they were arranging their target.

Kicking is already difficult enough in the perfect of circumstances. Disrupting an opposing kicker in subtle and perhaps subconscious ways could have a tangible impact on their success rate.

And the Patriots have seemingly benefited from big special teams moments through the years.

The supposed gamesmanship might also mean nothing. The fall and winter weather in New England often isn't that hospitable, so kickers will face cold and/or windy conditions.

Teams may have been aware of this already as well. Given how meticulously coaches prepare, surely somebody within the league flagged the Patriots' ploy, thus mitigating the effects.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Cardinals' Josh Sweat Amid Packers Buzz Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals are reportedly not looking to trade star pass-rusher Josh Sweat, but that doesn't necessarily mean it won't happen at some point during the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals are reportedly not looking to trade star pass-rusher Josh Sweat, but that doesn't necessarily mean it won't happen at some point during the 2026 NFL regular season.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , the Cardinals have told inquiring teams that they are not interested in trading Sweat, whom they have already paid a $7.22 million option bonus for this season.

Despite that, Graziano believes the Cards will continue to get calls on Sweat, and if they fall out of playoff contention prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, he could see Sweat's availability potentially changing.

Unsubstantiated rumors linked Sweat to the Green Bay Packers throughout the offseason, but Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst told reporters Tuesday that "somebody's making stuff up."

The 29-year-old Sweat is preparing to enter his second season as a member of the Cardinals after signing a four-year, $76.4 million deal with Arizona in free agency in 2025.

Sweat's first season with the Cards was a great one individually, as he set a new career high with 12 sacks, while also recording 30 tackles, 13 tackles for loss and four forced fumbles.

Despite that, the Cardinals did not thrive as a team, tying for the worst record in the NFL at 3-14.

Sweat is used to far more overall team success, as he reached the playoffs six times over his seven seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles.

That included a Super Bowl win in 2024, during which Sweat sacked Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes 2.5 times in Philly's 40-22 victory.

For his career, Sweat is a one-time Pro Bowler with 55 regular-season sacks and another five playoff sacks, making him a desirable target for contending teams in need of a pass-rush boost.

Per Graziano, Sweat is not due any guaranteed money beyond this year, and if a team were to trade for him midway through the 2026 season, they would only have to pay him about $5 million.

Given his history of production and reasonable contract, it is easy to envision the proverbial vultures circling the Cardinals and trying to pry Sweat away from them should they get off to a poor start this season.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on 'Clear Message' in Joey Porter Jr.'s Steelers Contract Extension Talks
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has considered both a trade request and holdout due to the slow pace of his contract negotiations, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has considered both a trade request and holdout due to the slow pace of his contract negotiations, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

Fowler reported Wednesday that "sources say the Steelers' lack of a formal offer for weeks sent the clear message to Porter that they would like him to play out the final year of his rookie contract, which prompted him to consider the possibility of a trade or sitting out for an extended period."

According to Fowler, "the Steelers most likely would do a deal with Porter" but may be dissuaded by a market in which top cornerbacks make more than $30 million per year.

"I'm told the new coaching staff is not a deterrent here. They are all-in on his ability as a high-level cover man," Fowler reported.

Porter told reporters Tuesday he felt he had "coaches and players really on my side that understand everything about the business side of things."

Tuesday marked Porter's first day back at practice following his absence from the majority of training camp and the preseason after being placed on the PUP list with a back injury in July.

The cornerback said Tuesday his back issues were the "whole reason" he had been sidelined.

He didn't offer a definitive answer, however, when asked if he would play in Week 1 without a new contract.

"I don't know. I have to talk to the guys upstairs, my agents, about that one," Porter said about the possibility of playing this season on an expiring deal (h/t ESPN's Brooke Pryor ).

Steelers general manager Omar Khan confirmed Monday the Steelers would not adjust their longstanding policy of not negotiating contracts in-season should Porter not agree to a new deal by Week 1.

Porter is currently set to enter the 2026 season carrying a $4.9 million cap hit in the final year of his rookie deal. As noted by Fowler, the projected franchise tag the Steelers could use to keep him under contract for 2027 would come out to about $23 million.

That tag is about $10 million below the top of the positional market, which Devon Witherspoon recently set at $33 million in average annual salary following his recent extension with the Seattle Seahawks.

Witherspoon is part of a group of five cornerbacks including the Cleveland Browns' Denzel Ward, Los Angeles Rams' Trent McDuffie, Indianapolis Colts' Sauce Gardner and Houston Texans' Derek Stingley Jr. who are set to make more than $30 million in average annual salary on their latest contracts.

Whether Porter is set on joining that group could impact the likelihood he and the Steelers are able to work out a new deal before opening the regular season Sunday, Sept. 13 against the visiting Atlanta Falcons.

articles.title: Chuba Hubbard, Jonathon Brooks' Panthers Usage Updated in NFL Rumors, Fantasy Impact, Draft Advice
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers have a pair of talented running backs in six-year veteran Chuba Hubbard and third-year speedster Jonathon Brooks, but their shared backfield creates a dilemma for fantasy football managers.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers have a pair of talented running backs in six-year veteran Chuba Hubbard and third-year speedster Jonathon Brooks, but their shared backfield creates a dilemma for fantasy football managers.

Brooks was selected in the second round of the 2024 draft, but he played in just three games as a rookie after suffering his second ACL tear in his right knee, and he missed the entire 2025 season while recovering. According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , Brooks' questionable durability gives Hubbard the edge as the Panthers' most dependable ball-carrier.

"They're excited about Brooks, but his health history means they will be extremely careful with him. He offers a lot of potential and explosiveness, but only if they can keep him on the field," Graziano explained. "That's why, to my understanding, the plan is for Hubbard and Brooks to split carries this season. If Hubbard stays healthy, he's the one in whom they've built up more trust, so I'd expect him to be the one the Panthers lean on to try to grind out games when they have the lead."

Hubbard recorded career highs of 1,195 yards and 10 touchdowns during Brooks' absence in 2024, but he was slowed by a calf injury last season that eventually cost him his starting role. He finished with just 511 yards and one rushing score while splitting carries with Rico Dowdle, who signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers in free agency.

Despite Hubbard's down year, Graziano pointed out that the Panthers "like Hubbard a lot -- as a runner, as a locker room leader, as many things." Brooks is expected to get a chance to prove his worth, but it still sounds like Carolina trusts Hubbard more.

"The split should be pretty close, but it would not be a surprise at all to get to the end of the season and see that Hubbard got the majority of the work," Graziano added.

Fantasy football managers should view both Hubbard and Brooks as boom-or-bust RB2 options. It's hard to justify drafting one of them without getting the security of also drafting the other, and it's far from ideal to dedicate two roster spots to players who play the same position on the same team.

For now, it appears that Hubbard would be the safer pick in fantasy drafts. Until Brooks can stay healthy, it won't be easy to depend on him without having a strong backup plan in place.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Mock Draft Analysis and Ideal Selection Strategy Cheat Sheet
articles.summary: With the NFL's 2026 season nearing its opener, fantasy football mock drafts will soon give way to fantasy football actual drafts.
articles.body:
With the NFL's 2026 season nearing its opener, fantasy football mock drafts will soon give way to fantasy football actual drafts.

In all of those leagues that haven't drafted yet, of course.

If you're in this boat, the water looks immaculate at the moment. Maybe things get stormy closer to you being on the clock, but for now, the forecast calls for sunshine, warmth and an entire offseason's worth of optimism.

By staying a step ahead, you can keep this calmness going into your draft. To help with that, let's continue the preparation process with a new three-round mock draft, analysis of the picks and cheat sheet rankings to help you form the ideal selection strategy.

Even for a PPR league, this mock placed a heavy premium on pass-catchers. A.J. Brown cracked the top 10, and Jonathan Taylor didn't. Those were certainly the biggest surprises of the first round, and they were setting the tone for what was to come.

Mock drafters had to decide whether to pay the tax on pass-catchers or take discounts elsewhere but risk being frozen out on receivers or tight ends. Most teams did the former. Seven of the first 10 picks were receivers; save for Lamar Jackson, the third round was comprised entirely of receivers and tight ends (including a surprise selection of Colston Loveland).

Running back values were easily found. Chase Brown, Saquon Barkley and Kenneth Walker III closing out the second round as the 22nd, 23rd and 24th picks, respectively, highlighted that pretty perfectly. Then again, when the fourth round arrived with the likes of Jeremiyah Love, Kyren Williams and Javonte Williams on the board, managers who hammered the pass-catching positions early had to be thrilled with their options at running back.

When a position or two is being pushed up the board, it's always a delicate dance deciding between the climbing costs or the bargain buys elsewhere. Consistently paying above cost hardly feels like a formula for success, but the same goes for letting everyone else pick apart a position that you haven't addressed.

articles.title: "The community has given back so much to me": How Patrick Mahomes is repaying Kansas City - One scholarship, playground, and grant at a time
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes earned his Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year nomination the hard way. Not with a single headline moment, but with nearly $2.75 million.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes earned his Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year nomination the hard way. Not with a single headline moment, but with nearly $2.75 million in grants distributed through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, a rebuilt park named after Martin Luther King Jr., thousands of meals delivered to food-insecure families, and scholarship checks written for kids whose parents never went to college. Kansas City gave Mahomes a platform. He has been spending it generously ever since.What has Patrick Mahomes done for the Kansas City community through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation?Patrick Mahomes established the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019, with a focus on improving the lives of children through health, wellness, and support for communities in need. Since then, the scope has widened considerably.To date, nearly $2.75 million in grants has been distributed through the foundation, and the Kansas City Business Journal has ranked it among the city's biggest charitable trusts and foundations by grant volume. That is not a vanity number. It represents food drives, free eye exams, school literacy programs, and youth football equipment for teams that could not afford it otherwise.Through partnerships with food banks, the foundation has distributed more than 15,000 meals. A separate literacy push, the Read for 15 program, brought in more than 19,000 student pledges and produced a 12 percent increase in reading scores at participating schools. These are not soft statistics. They reflect programs designed to return something measurable to neighborhoods that often get overlooked.Mahomes has been direct about why Kansas City specifically. "Brittany and I take great pride in the platform we have to give back to a community that has given us so much over the last six years," he said. That line lands differently when you trace what the foundation has actually built.What is the MLK Jr. Park project that Patrick Mahomes funded in Kansas City?One moment stands above the rest in terms of scale and symbolism. Mahomes and his foundation re-dedicated Kansas City's Martin Luther King Jr. Park at a ceremony that fell exactly 58 years after King's "I Have a Dream" speech. The moment was made possible by a $1 million donation from 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, funding a playground designed through community engagement sessions with the goal of being inclusive and accessible for children of all abilities.A million dollars toward a public park. Not a naming rights deal. Not a corporate partnership announcement. Just money directed into a neighborhood space where kids can actually use it.Mahomes also hosted a OneSight Vision Clinic that provided free eye exams and glasses to more than 100 children in the Kansas City area, and through his foundation's wellness program, he helped encourage dental screenings throughout Kansas City schools in Kansas. These are the kinds of investments that rarely generate national headlines but matter enormously to the families receiving them.What is the "15 for 15" program and how does it help underserved youth?The foundation's "15 for 15" programming has supported groups in a wide range of ways, including sending underserved youth to Chiefs games and to football games at Mahomes' alma mater, Texas Tech; funding adoptions for rescue dogs; covering art-focused after-school programs; funding Camp Hope scholarships for youth battling cancer; outfitting youth football teams with equipment and jerseys; and supporting athletes competing in Special Olympics.The breadth of it is intentional. Mahomes has spoken about understanding financial uncertainty from his own upbringing, and the 15 for 15 model reflects that. He described the recognition as meaningful beyond just himself: "To be recognized for such a prestigious award means the world to me and I'm thankful to represent my foundation, Walter Payton and his family, the Hunt family, this team and all of Chiefs Kingdom on such a significant stage."Mahomes also partnered with RISE to Vote ahead of the 2020 general election and worked with the Hunt Family Foundation to convert Arrowhead Stadium into the largest polling center in Kansas City Election Board history, serving more than 2,100 voters. Community investment, for Mahomes, clearly extends beyond charity into civic participation.The on-field legacy is already set. Three Super Bowls, multiple MVPs, a contract that will keep him in red and gold for years. What is being built off the field in Kansas City, quietly and consistently, may prove just as enduring.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The Rams think they've figured out jet lag. Australia is about to test their theory
articles.summary: The Rams and 49ers are about to embark on the longest road trip in NFL history. They've also come up with radically different ideas for how to survive it.
articles.body:
Ten months ago, the Los Angeles Rams conducted an audacious experiment.

They sought to reduce the toll that transatlantic travel takes on players' bodies by approaching a game in London like a hit-and-run mission.

Instead of flying out a few days before kickoff the way most NFL teams do, the Rams arrived in London just a day before facing the Jacksonville Jaguars and began their journey home soon after the final whistle. There would be no need for body clocks to adapt to the eight-hour time difference, the Rams theorized, if the trip was as short as possible.

Poking holes in the Rams' tactics became harder over the course of a crisp 35-7 pummeling of a Jaguars team that lost only three other games last regular season. "The way the guys played showed it was the right decision," Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters after his team brushed off the absence of injured star receiver Puka Nakua, charged to a 21-0 halftime lead and coasted to a blowout victory.

Emboldened by last year's successful trial run, the Rams are getting even more daring. They're applying the same philosophy to the longest trip in NFL history, a 16-hour flight to Melbourne, Australia, covering nearly 8,000 miles. Australia hosts its first regular-season NFL game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Friday, Sept. 11, when the Super Bowl favorite Rams open their season against the San Francisco 49ers. Kickoff is at 10:35 a.m. in Melbourne so that the game airs in prime time on Thursday, Sept. 10, back in the U.S.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

The Rams plan to fly into Melbourne the day before the game and fly out immediately after, ESPN reported last month . Neither McVay nor team officials have been willing to confirm the team's travel itinerary, but the Rams head coach recently admitted to reporters, "We're leaving later than most people would probably expect."

The 49ers, conversely, are leaving for Melbourne on Sept. 2, a full week ahead of kickoff to give themselves as long as possible to recharge after a long travel day and adjust to the 17-hour time difference. The drastically different approaches have captured the attention of sleep scientists who study athletic performance and sparked spirited debate over which is preferable.

"The Rams will win the game," predicted neurologist and sleep specialist W. Christopher Winter with Joe Namath-like confidence. The basis for Winter's guarantee is not the strength of the Rams' star-laden roster but the timing of their last-minute arrival in Melbourne.

To Winter, the 49ers' decision to fly in early and acclimate to the time difference could backfire because of the morning kickoff time in Melbourne. The timing of the game, Winter said, favors the team whose body clocks are still on Pacific Time rather than the one who has already spent a week in Australia.

"Athletes generally reach their physical peak in the late afternoon and early evening," said Winter, a sleep consultant to more than a dozen teams across American professional sports.

"So what the Rams are essentially doing is saying to their players, 'Look, just keep being athletically awesome at 6 p.m. You're going to open your eyes one day and the sun's going to be in a weird part of the sky, but we're banking on it taking your brain a couple days to figure out what the hell's going on. By then you'll have already beaten the 49ers and you'll be heading home.'''

The kickoff time is favorable to the Rams, Dr. Meeta Singh conceded, but the Michigan-based sleep specialist argued that the downsides to a last-minute arrival in Melbourne far outweigh the potential benefits. Several times during a phone conversation with Yahoo Sports, Singh said she was curious "what the Rams were thinking to come to the conclusion that this travel plan is their best option."

The way Singh sees it, the Rams risk playing the game at a major sleep deficit by journeying to Australia so close to kickoff time. It's difficult for most people to get anywhere close to a full eight hours of sleep on a plane, Singh argued, even an NFL charter flight that no doubt features recliners or lie-flat seats designed to accommodate the massive frames of professional football players.

"The issue is whether they're going to get enough sleep the several days before the game," said Singh, who has served as a sleep optimization consultant for NFL franchises and for other college and professional teams. "If you're exhausted or sleep-deprived, your performance slips. That's the worst-case scenario."

NFL teams have always hunted for opportunities to gain a microscopic competitive advantage over their opponents, but for decades sleep science went overlooked. While nutrition, hydration and strength training and conditioning became part of players' daily regimen, teams seldom prioritized optimal sleep to the same degree.

In 2011, sleep physician and performance specialist Cheri D. Mah and a team of fellow Stanford researchers published a groundbreaking study demonstrating that optimal sleep is a key factor in peak athletic performance. Mah and her colleagues asked Stanford basketball players to aim to sleep 10 hours per night for a period of 5 to 7 weeks. At the end of that sleep extension period, the players collectively sprinted faster, shot more accurately and reported improved performance in practices and games.

Subsequent studies by Mah and others in her field found that elite athletes often competed while sleep-deprived and travel-weary and their performance suffered as a result. Those athletes displayed a range of symptoms, from impaired judgment, to slower reaction times, to reduced speed, precision and endurance, to greater susceptibility to injury or illness.

"It's not even just like having a beer," Mah said. "There's actually a study that shows if you are awake 17 hours, your reaction time is impaired to the same level as being legally intoxicated in the United States."

Eyes opened by the new research, savvy NFL teams began exploring how they could gain a potential competitive edge by altering their travel and practice schedules to optimize how players and coaches slept. Inexpensive methods of monitoring sleep and recovery also hastened the NFL's sleep science revolution, as did the increase in international travel as the league sought to grow its global fan base in strategic markets.

"Sleep is a weapon," Mah often says when speaking directly to NFL players. She recommends they get 8-to-10 hours of sleep per night, urging them to accelerate time-zone acclimatization by going to bed an hour or two earlier in the days leading up to a west-to-east flight and by getting plenty of early morning sunlight upon arrival.

When advising NFL teams, Mah recommends treating travel as a performance tool by designing the itinerary around circadian biology. Teams taking charter planes to international games can reinforce the shift in body clock they're seeking by better timing their mid-flight sleep and meals. Mah also recommends teams provide eye masks, noise control and other tools to help players maximize sleep quality.

"I truly believe that sleep and body-clock strategy is still one of the most untapped competitive advantages in sports," Mah said. "Teams that are leveraging these strategies are going to have such an advantage over those that haven't thought about them."

When asked specifically about the NFL's first Australia game next week, Mah said there are pros and cons to the travel itineraries of both the Rams and 49ers.

The kickoff time favors the Rams' approach of trying to stay on Pacific Time, according to Mah, but the 49ers can mitigate that disadvantage by practicing at 10:30 a.m. in Melbourne once they arrive. Travel fatigue from the 16-hour flight will work against the Rams, but they too can reduce the damage by banking sleep before the trip, appropriately timing meals and sleep and controlling light on board the plane and at the team hotel.

Ultimately, Mah is a pragmatist. She knows how fans will decide whether the Rams or 49ers had the smarter travel plan.

"Whoever wins," Mah said with a laugh, "that's what will be considered the right strategy."

articles.title: NFL Trade Rumors: Did Steelers’ ‘clear message’ push Joey Porter Jr. toward a holdout or trade request?
articles.summary: NFL News: Joey Porter Jr. reportedly received a message from the Pittsburgh Steelers without the team having to say much at all.ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported We.
articles.body: Joey Porter Jr. reportedly received a message from the Pittsburgh Steelers without the team having to say much at all.ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that Pittsburgh’s failure to make a formal contract offer for weeks prompted Porter to consider requesting a trade or sitting out for an extended period. With Week 1 approaching, the Steelers’ own contract policy has turned a slow negotiation into a deadline.Why did Joey Porter Jr. consider a trade request or holdout before Week 1?According to Fowler, the Steelers’ lack of movement left Porter with a clear impression about how Pittsburgh wanted to handle the final year of his rookie contract.“Sources say the Steelers' lack of a formal offer for weeks sent the clear message to Porter that they would like him to play out the final year of his rookie contract, which prompted him to consider the possibility of a trade or sitting out for an extended period,” Fowler reported.That does not mean Pittsburgh wants Porter gone.Fowler also reported that “the Steelers most likely would do a deal with Porter,” while adding that the rising cornerback market could complicate negotiations.The coaching staff also appears to want Porter in Pittsburgh.“I'm told the new coaching staff is not a deterrent here. They are all-in on his ability as a high-level cover man,” Fowler reported.Porter returned to practice Tuesday after spending most of training camp and the preseason sidelined. He had been placed on the physically unable to perform list because of a back injury in July.Porter told reporters that the injury was the “whole reason” for his absence. His answer about playing without an extension, however, created another issue.Asked whether he would play on his expiring contract, Porter did not commit.“I don't know,” Porter said. “I got to talk to the guys upstairs and my agents about that.”Minutes earlier, Porter initially sounded more certain when asked whether he would play if healthy.“Yeah, for sure,” he said before pausing and adding, “maybe.”That uncertainty matters because Pittsburgh does not have much time to resolve it.What is stopping the Steelers from giving Joey Porter Jr. a new contract?Money sits at the center of the discussion.Porter is entering the final year of his rookie deal with a $4.9 million cap hit. Meanwhile, the top of the cornerback market has moved well beyond $30 million in average annual salary.Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon recently set the mark at $33 million per year. Denzel Ward, Trent McDuffie, Sauce Gardner and Derek Stingley Jr. are also set to average more than $30 million annually on their latest deals.Fowler reported that those numbers could make Pittsburgh hesitant.The Steelers also have another option if Porter plays out the season. The projected franchise tag for a cornerback in 2027 is roughly $23 million, according to Over the Cap. That figure sits about $10 million below Witherspoon’s annual average.Pittsburgh has already extended three players from Porter’s 2023 draft class. Nick Herbig, Darnell Washington and Keeanu Benton received new deals while Porter continues to wait.Porter said he was happy for his teammates.“I was really just happy that they got theirs done,” Porter said. “I came in with those guys, me, Herb, and Keeanu and even Washington, we all came in together. Those are my guys. So I was ecstatic that they got paid.”His own negotiations have been harder.“It's been tough, not going to lie,” Porter said. “It's my first go around [with] this.”Steelers general manager Omar Khan added another clock to the situation Monday. Pittsburgh will maintain its longstanding policy of refusing to negotiate contracts once the regular season begins.That makes Sept. 13 significant for more than the Steelers’ opener against the Atlanta Falcons.If Porter and Pittsburgh cannot reach an agreement before Week 1, contract talks could effectively stop until after the season. Porter has not promised he will play without a new deal.For now, Pittsburgh still has its starting cornerback back at practice. Whether it has him under a new contract, or even committed to playing Week 1, remains unresolved.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tony Romo's moment of truth has nothing to do with a broadcast booth
articles.summary: Romo's future in the CBS booth is suddenly in serious jeopardy, but that may be the least important part of what's happening to him.
articles.body:
It says something about the world we now inhabit that most initial reactions to Tony Romo's July arrest for operating a vehicle under the influence focused on his future as a broadcaster, and whether CBS would use this as a pretext for getting out from under Romo's massive contract.

That's natural, of course. We always process news first for how it affects us personally; it's why so many people use a celebrity's death to mention the time they met the recently-deceased. Romo has been a fixture in NFL fans' lives for the last decade as an announcer, an occasionally inspiring, often maddening, always provocative presence in the booth. He's one of the few people who has the honor of speaking directly to tens of millions of NFL viewers every Sunday.

And now, he needs help. Because he might have just thrown all that away on one Wisconsin roadside.

Two new developments in Romo's OWI case Tuesday change the trajectory of this story. First, Romo himself put out what certainly reads like a heartfelt statement on his arrest and current state of mind. Noting that he pleaded no contest to the OWI charge, he added:

"Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol."

The arrest and public humiliation, Romo noted, "required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public. I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes."

Good on Romo for taking that responsibility, even if, like most statements, his reads like it was crafted by public relations agents. Not so good was the news that followed shortly thereafter, that Romo's blood alcohol content at the time of his arrest was 0.15, nearly twice Wisconsin's legal limit of 0.08.

That figure alone is bad enough; combined with Romo's admission of "over-reliance on alcohol," it's a devastating indictment of where he is now in his personal life. The public acknowledgement of guilt and responsibility is a big step, but only the first one. You only need to look at Tiger Woods to see the damage that can be done when someone who doesn't belong behind a wheel gets back on the road again and again.

Romo was already struggling to keep pace with the changing tides of NFL broadcasting. Unlike play-by-play callers such as Romo's CBS partner Jim Nantz and Al Michaels, color analysts must be, well, colorful. For Romo, that initially meant analyzing formations and predicting plays before they happened; since that illustrious start, he's devolved into a quirky caricature of himself.

Romo now slings gaffes like a rookie throwing interceptions, and CBS is surely wary of the social media blowback — and arrest video GIFs — that would surface whenever Romo gets a little too excited or throws down an ice-cold take.

Romo signed a massive contract in 2020, a 10-year, $180 million deal that still has an astounding $72 million yet to run. That's not his fault; blame whoever negotiated that deal at CBS. But now, perhaps sensing an opportunity to cut loose that massive deal, CBS is offering less-than-full-throated support of Romo in his current travails.

"We have to consider the impact on our image and our brand," CBS Sports president David Berson said at last month's "NFL on CBS" media day, when asked about Romo's fate. He termed the Romo matter an "evolving situation" — corporate-speak for "all options are on the table" — and avoided putting a timetable on Romo's fate. In the meantime, CBS has promoted J.J. Watt into Romo's seat alongside Nantz.

Like a quarterback who doesn't pick up on a blitz until it's too late, Romo, 46, is a victim of changing times, a prisoner of his own clichés in the booth and mistakes outside it. Here's hoping he asks for, and gets, the help he needs.

articles.title: Why one detail about NFL final rosters proves former Florida coach Billy Napier was worse than you remember
articles.summary: The 4-8 Florida Gators produced nine players on NFL 53-man rosters, matching Alabama and Georgia despite Billy Napier's disastrous final season.
articles.body: All 32 NFL teams made their final cuts to trim their active rosters down to 53 men earlier this week, a sign that football is slowly but surely coming back into our lives. With rosters being finalized, it also means we can see how many rookies ended up making it to the NFL, and all the usual suspects are well represented. The Ohio State Buckeyes led the way with 11 rookies from the 2026 Draft class on NFL rosters, followed by Texas A&M, which had 10 former Aggies make it to the league. Those two make sense, considering they dominate the recruiting rankings year in and year out and both made the College Football Playoff this past season. Other mainstays like Alabama and Georgia were right behind the Aggies and Buckeyes with nine rookies on NFL rosters, but another team that hasn't even sniffed the CFP in the last several years was hilariously lumped in with the rest of these upper echelon college programs. THE 5 MOST DISAPPOINTING PRESEASON TOP-10 COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS OF THE 21ST CENTURY That's right, folks! The 4-8 Florida Gators produced a staggering nine players from their 2025 football team that ended up on 53-man rosters in the NFL. Talk about doing less with more, right? And yes, there are some qualifiers that need to be thrown out there about these players. One is a long snapper, and while it's important to have a good long snapper, it doesn't exactly move the needle in the win-loss column. The other is Caleb Banks who, while being a first-round pick, only played in three games for Florida in 2025. But, when you couple that with the fact that a lot of Florida's best players weren't even draft eligible this past April - like All-SEC running back Jadan Baugh, Freshman All-SEC wideout Vernell Brown III, sack leader and Freshman All-SEC edge rusher Jayden Woods, and leading tackler/All-SEC linebacker Myles Graham - you start to see just how disappointing this team was this past season. And it starts at the top. Head coach Billy Napier took a team loaded with NFL talent and a five-star quarterback under center in DJ Lagway and led the Gators to the worst possible outcome. Seriously, if you gave that Gators team an average coach and simulated the season 1,000 times, I don't think he would do worse than 4-8 unless his entire roster spontaneously combusted. Florida's in-state rivals, the Miami Hurricanes, also had nine rookie players make an NFL roster this week, and that team played for a national championship just this past season in addition to embarrassing the Gators the two times they met up on the field in 2024 and 2025. Asking this team to go out and win a national title might be a bridge too far, but Florida was a darkhorse Playoff contender this time a year ago. And the Gators didn't even make a bowl game. This is why Napier is no longer employed by the University of Florida, but it's a good reminder of why Gators athletic director Scott Stricklin probably should have pulled the trigger sooner. While most of its peers with regard to roster talent were out here winning 10 games and making the CFP, Florida won a whopping two SEC games and lost to South Florida in The Swamp. Think about that for a second. How many USF Bulls do you see on NFL rosters this week? I rest my case. Florida's impressive NFL presence only highlights how incompetent the Napier regime was, but it's also a silver lining for Gator fans. If new head coach Jon Sumrall and his staff are even competent coaches, supporters of the program won't have to endure rock bottom for too much longer. Again, is it fair to expect a national championship right away? STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW! No. But a seven or eight-win season and a nice bowl game would be a great start, which, ironically enough, represented Napier's ceiling. Coaching matters, and if you want proof, look no further than the 2025 Florida Gators. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And after you're done looking, try not to run to your toilet and puke.

articles.title: Browns GM Makes Cryptic Remark About QB Trade Offers Amid Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel Buzz
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns assistant general manager Catherine Hickman declined to provide any insight when asked whether the team received trade offers for its quarterbacks.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns assistant general manager Catherine Hickman declined to provide any insight when asked whether the team received trade offers for its quarterbacks.

"Not that I will comment on," she told reporters Wednesday while deferring to GM Andrew Berry:

Hickman's follow-up could be an important distinction.

Her initial remark on its own would lead some fans to assume the Browns did get offers for one or more of Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green. The fact they're all four still on the roster would elicit its own conclusions.

But Hickman may have intended to avoid saying yes or no, leaving the topic for her boss to address at a later date.

It's safe to assume Watson's contract made him untradeable. The Browns would've had to carry a lot of dead money to make that happen, and his $40.2 million salary cap hit is a sizable sum to absorb for a quarterback who hasn't played in a year and a half.

Sanders battled Watson for the starting job and is the closest thing Cleveland has to a viable long-term solution. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in his eight appearances as a rookie. Trading him right now wouldn't make a lot of sense.

That leaves Gabriel, whom ESPN's Jeremy Fowler suggested could've had a market. But now the southpaw is on injured reserve and ineligible to suit up for the first four games.

With Gabriel on IR, the Browns are heading into the regular season with three active QBs: Watson, Sanders and Green. Once Gabriel is healthy and they're facing the prospect of adding one more to the mix, something might give.

For now, the front office is probably tuning out any outside trade chatter, if it exists in the first place.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Named Raiders' QB1 Over Fernando Mendoza for NFL Week 1 vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will have to wait a bit before getting his first taste of regular season action in the NFL.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will have to wait a bit before getting his first taste of regular season action in the NFL.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak announced on Wednesday that veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins will be the starter over Mendoza for the team's Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 13.

Kubiak added that he spoke with Raiders minority owner Tom Brady "multiple times a week" before making the decision.

As ESPN's Adam Schefter pointed out, the Raiders' decision to have Mendoza start the year on the bench snaps a streak of six straight quarterbacks who were named the starter on opening day after being drafted No. 1 overall.

Kubiak addressed how Mendoza's development will be affected by being named Cousins' backup.

"There's always early work, late work, more meetings, plenty of time on the field between drills with Coach [Mike] Sullivan and Coach [Andrew] Janocko. Every player that is not starting the first game, they're helping us on the look team," Kubiak said, per Sam Warren of The Athletic. "We're just trying to find every edge we can find to continue to get him better and his teammates better."

The Raiders signed Cousins to a reported five-year, $172 million contract that, in reality, is a one-year, fully guaranteed $20 million deal. After Las Vegas entered the offseason with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 draft, it was clear that the plan was to have Cousins as the bridge quarterback before handing the reins to Mendoza. The team also has fourth-year backup signal-caller Aidan O'Connell to provide extra insurance.

"He played really good football," Kubiak said of Cousins, per team reporter Levi Edwards . "I'm really happy with all three of our quarterbacks. Kirk's had a really good offseason, very good camp and he's earned it."

The Raiders are not expected to contend for a playoff spot in the competitive AFC this season, so there will likely be a point where they insert Mendoza as the starter to give him some experience in his rookie year. For now, the 22-year-old will focus on learning from Cousins as he leads the way to start the season.

articles.title: Former Eagles staffer finds another way the Bill Belichick Patriots tried to gain an advantage over opponents
articles.summary: The Patriots of the Bill Belichick era already have Spygate and Deflategate on their resume.
articles.body:
Bill Belichick's New England Patriots' teams proved they would do whatever it takes to win championships. For all the excellence of their individual players, coaches and coordinators, the Patriots teams of that era are no stranger to controversy.

First, it was Spygate and Deflategate. Now, it's … uh Scoreboardgate?

Ryan Paganetti, a former Philadelphia Eagles staffer, posted a thread on X detailing how the Patriots would mess with opposing kickers during the Belichick era.

As Paganetti explained, when opposing kickers were lining up for a field goal at Gillette Stadium, the Patriots' scoreboard team would show a reversed image of the goalpost on the scoreboard to try and mess with the kicker's head.

As you can see from the images Paganetti used in his post, the tactic creates a situation where four uprights appear in the kicker's line of sight. And since the images were reversed, the scoreboard video could play tricks on the kicker, as the wind flags would blow in the opposite direction on the scoreboard.

Paganetti said he reviewed 52 field goals from 2012-2020, and all the clips he posted were from the Belichick era.

Paganetti added that the Patriots did not utilize the same tactic when their kickers attempted field goals at Gillette Stadium. He even said the Eagles tried to utilize the same tactic, but the location of the video boards at Lincoln Financial Field "made it nearly useless."

How effective was that strategy for the Patriots? Paganetti claimed away field goal percentage during the Belichick era was the lowest in the league and that the margin between Patriots kickers and their opponents was the highest in the league.

That certainly seems to suggest the Patriots benefitted in a major way from the tactic, though it's worth mentioning other reasons that may have played a role in opposing kickers missing against New England.

From a weather perspective, playing in New England, especially in the winter months, almost certainly played a role in some of those misses. Patriots kickers would be far more accustomed to how the wind affects kicks at home.

The team's dominance in the era likely also played a role. Once the Patriots emerged as a dynasty, that put extra pressure on opposing kickers in big moments. And since Gillette Stadium hosted a lot of home playoff games, that pressure likely multiplied in those instances.

It also helps that the Patriots benefitted from having Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri kicking for them for a decent portion of that era. After him, the team utilized Stephen Gostkowski, whose numbers present an intriguing Hall of Fame case.

Those caveats aren't going to stop some from piling on the Patriots. But before you do that, it's worth noting that one kicker from the same era said New England was far from the only team engaging in those shenanigans.

Pro Bowler Graham Gano said teams would use various tactics to throw opposing kickers off their game.

Given that — and the fact that the legality of the tactic is unclear and it happened under a previous coaching regime — it's unlikely the Patriots face punishment from the strategy. The NFL may not even feel compelled to respond to questions on the topic.

While Belichick might even get a question about it during a North Carolina press conference, he's never been one to shed light on details like this, even though he typically loves talking special teams .

Ultimately, Paganetti discovered a new — at least to the public — way the Patriots tried to rig the system to their advantage back in the day. It's unlikely that revelation has an impact on how the league operates today, but it's still a fascinating discovery, one that reinforces Belichick and Co. were going to take every single advantage possible to gain an edge over their competition.

articles.title: NFL to commemorate 25th anniversary of 9/11 terrorist attacks across all its stadiums and even in Australia
articles.summary: The NFL will stencil "Never Forget" in every end zone and auction special 9/11 tribute coins as all Week 1 games mark the terror attacks' 25th anniversary.
articles.body: Sometimes the NFL does the right thing. And the league's intention to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks so that its fans do not forget what happened is one such instance. America's most popular league and its 32 clubs will honor the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001, through a series of commemorative efforts in communities across the globe. "We continue to honor the memory of those we lost on September 11 and the heroes whose courage and sacrifice inspired our nation," NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement on Wednesday. "Out of unimaginable tragedy emerged an extraordinary sense of unity and service that brought Americans together. 9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS "As the NFL family reflects on this day 25 years later, we remember those who were taken from us and support those who continue to carry the pain of that day. We also recommit ourselves to the spirit of resilience, community, and service that remains an enduring example for future generations." The NFL says all Week 1 games will feature tributes designed to honor the lives lost, recognize survivors, first responders and military families, and connect fans to the lasting message of remembrance and service that emerged after September 11. FOX NATION, TUNNEL TO TOWERS EXPLORES HOW AMERICA’S PASTIME HELPED A GRIEVING NEW YORK HEAL AFTER 9/11 NFL clubs will participate through in-stadium moments, broadcast integrations – including live national anthem coverage across 1 p.m. ET games – and community engagement efforts throughout the week. OutKick first reported over the weekend that the league will have clubs stencil "Never Forget" in stadium end zones the first week of the season. And, yes, those will go away after Week 1 and be replaced by other messaging. Game officials will use special 9/11 tribute-branded coins for the pregame toss. Those coins will later be auctioned on the NFL Auction platform to benefit the league’s September 11 charitable partners. When the New York Giants host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, mere miles from where the Twin Towers were attacked by Muslim terrorists who flew planes into the building, players, coaches and staff from both teams will wear commemorative NYPD, FDNY and PAPD hats on the sideline in recognition of the first responders who served and died on 9/11 and in the days that followed. Players and coaches from both teams will also wear special 9/11-branded "Never Forget" T-shirts during pregame warmups. Giants-branded versions of the caps will be available for purchase at the team store, with proceeds benefiting the respective agencies. The NFL is even taking its 9/11 ceremonies abroad. During the NFL’s first-ever regular season game in Australia, pregame ceremonies will honor the 25th anniversary of 9/11 with U.S. and Australian color guards and large-field flag presentations featuring U.S. Marines, Navy personnel and Australian service members. Through its Salute to Service partnership with TAPS, the NFL Foundation will also support weeklong activities for military families of the fallen with a connection to 9/11, including a ceremony at Melbourne’s Shrine of Remembrance and on-field recognition before the game. The NFL says it is doing all this to "honor those affected by the tragedy and reaffirm its commitment to preserving the lessons and legacy of that day for years to come." articles.title: Colin Kaepernick believes Jay-Z has a ‘guilty conscience’ over deals with NFL and Target
articles.summary: Kaepernick made the comments as part of an extensive interview with NBC News ahead of the release of his memoir, “The Perilous Fight.”
articles.body: Colin Kaepernick said he believes that Jay-Z’s recent comments about him speak to a “guilty conscience,” as the fallout between the former quarterback and the rapper deepens. Kaepernick responded as part of an extensive interview with NBC News after Jay-Z dissed the athlete during a recent concert. In July, Jay-Z took aim at Kaepernick, the former San Francisco 49ers star, mentioning him and his settlement with the NFL in an impromptu rap during a series of concerts at Yankee Stadium. “They run out of characters, had to bring back up [Kaepernick] again,” Jay-Z said, referring to people who have criticized him for a recent partnership with Target. “Buddy took a check, I ain’t even mad at him, but along with that check you have to sign a non-disparagement. I’m the one [the NFL] can’t control.” Earlier this year, Jay-Z drew ire when it was announced that he would sell an exclusive version of his “Reasonable Doubt” album at the retailer, which has been subjected to boycotts by Black shoppers after it rolled back its diversity, equity and inclusion practices. Kaepernick, on the other hand, is honoring the boycott despite the potential financial cost. A spokesperson for the former quarterback confirmed he would not be selling his upcoming memoir, “The Perilous Fight,” in Target stores. Target did not immediately respond to requests for comment. For his book tour, Kaepernick is partnering with the National Association of Black Bookstores. Jay-Z was freestyling about the hypocrisy of his critics in July when he mentioned Kaepernick. The lyrics were a far cry from 2017, when Jay-Z dedicated a performance of his song “The Story of O.J.” to Kaepernick after he had taken a knee to protest police brutality in America. At the time, Kaepernick was a free agent. He never found employment in the NFL again after he protested during the national anthem in the 2016 season. Jay-Z, who wore Kaepernick’s jersey during a performance on “Saturday Night Live” in 2017, was one of Kaepernick’s highest-profile supporters. Jay-Z was critical of the NFL, rapping on the 2018 song “Apes---” with his wife, Beyoncé, “I said no to the Super Bowl. You need me; I don’t need you.” In his book, Kaepernick wrote that Jay-Z asked him in 2017 to kneel onstage during a performance of “The Story of O.J.” but that he declined, in part because he objected to the use of racial slurs in the lyrics. Kaepernick also wrote that before he was asked to join Jay-Z onstage, he had difficulties connecting with him on the phone as they exchanged emails in an effort to join forces on social justice issues. Their relationship flipped in August 2019, when Jay-Z announced that Roc Nation, the entertainment company he co-founded, would partner with the NFL. Roc Nation has since produced every Super Bowl halftime show, and it partners with the league on social justice work. Roc Nation declined to comment to NBC News for this article. In his book, Kaepernick wrote that Jay-Z told him about the partnership only after it had been agreed to, and Kaepernick expressed his displeasure. “I just want you to know, one, you’re serving the culture up to a bunch of racists and, two, they don’t care about you,” Kaepernick wrote about what he told Jay-Z when they spoke. “You’re the music guy to them. They quite literally need a Black face—and have said as much.” In 2019, Jay-Z faced blowback for the NFL deal, as many viewed it as his turning his back on Kaepernick, who remained unemployed by the league. At a news conference announcing the partnership, Jay-Z defended the decision. “I think we have moved past kneeling. I think it’s time for action,” he said. “We forget that Colin’s whole thing was to bring attention to social injustice. In that case, this is a success. This is the next phase.” The NFL declined to comment. Kaepernick, who told NBC News’ Lester Holt that he did not sign a non-disparagement agreement with the NFL after having settled in 2019 with the league over his collusion lawsuit, said several people sent him the video of the freestyle. “First and foremost, what it speaks to is power of people,” Kaepernick said about his reaction. “The backlash that [Jay-Z] received for partnering with the NFL and going counter to people’s interests in 2019 was a major problem for him, so much so that he’s still bringing it up in 2026.” He added: “People are now realizing, ‘Why are you so comfortable stepping into these positions that are counter to the positions that people on the ground actually want?’ And to me, I view that as speaking to a guilty conscience and trying to reposition or reframe the conversation.” Kaepernick said people who supported him have been consistent in not agreeing with Jay-Z’s actions. “I haven’t publicly spoken about him in any matter, but it speaks to the level of impact that people are having and being able to continue to move not only individuals but corporations,” he said. As for why he didn’t respond to Jay-Z immediately after the freestyle, particularly in regard to the misinformation about a non-disparagement agreement, Kaepernick said that there have always been efforts to discredit him and that Jay-Z is “another player” in that effort since he partnered with the NFL. “He has built the alignment with the NFL, the NFL that has blackballed me, the same NFL that, in a players-owners meeting in 2017, said we need a Black face to help us get rid of the protests,” Kaepernick told NBC News. (The NFL has long denied Kaepernick’s blackballing claims.) Kaepernick added: “I understand why he’s trying to do reputational recovery. I get it. I don’t agree with the actions, but I’m also not gonna respond to everything that’s said about me, because I also believe the actions and the work that I do will speak for themselves.”

articles.title: Raiders name Kirk Cousins as Week 1 starting quarterback, Fernando Mendoza will begin career as backup
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders named Kirk Cousins the team's starting quarterback on Wednesday, meaning No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza will begin his career as a backup.
articles.body: Mendoza-Mania will not be coming to Las Vegas just yet. Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak announced Wednesday that the team is naming Kirk Cousins its Week 1 starting quarterback against the Miami Dolphins, meaning Fernando Mendoza will begin his career as a backup. "(Cousins has) played really good football, I’m really happy with all three of (the) quarterbacks. Kirk’s had a really good offseason, very good camp, and he’s earned it," Kubiak told reporters. When asked if he expects Mendoza to play at all this year, Kubiak deflected the question and said the team is focused on the Dolphins. Raiders general manager John Spytek and minority owner Tom Brady have been advocates about letting a rookie develop behind a veteran quarterback, which makes the team's decision to roll with Cousins unsurprising. Spytek said Mendoza has shown the team everything it learned about him in the draft process when talking to reporters Tuesday. "He’s a tireless worker. He loves football. He loves his teammates. He’s energetic on the field. He’s self-critical. He’s self-aware. He’s very accurate," Spytek said during a recent press conference. "His time is coming, but he’s got to earn it every day, and he knows that. I think we’re all very pleased with the person and his work ethic and his commitment to being a great quarterback." When asked if the team has a proof of concept for how to best develop a young quarterback, Spytek cited examples from multiple different processes. "Tom Brady, Aaron Rodgers, Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, but Jayden Daniels. Like you said, there’s success stories and failures in both ways," Spytek said. "We’re just trying to build the best team we can and play the guys that are most ready to play, and have a constant competition in every room, not just the quarterback room, but every room." Brady, Rodgers, Love and Mahomes all sat during their rookie years and, in some cases, multiple seasons before taking over starting jobs and flourishing. Daniels, however, started as a rookie and thrived, winning The Associated Press NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and making the Pro Bowl after leading the Commanders to the NFC championship game. Kubiak said Brady has been a great resource for the team when it comes to making the decision on the team's starting quarterback. articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Vikings Future, Injury Status Updated by GM Nolan Teasley Ahead of Week 1
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are expecting quarterback J.J. McCarthy to be on their Week 1 roster, general manager Nolan Teasley confirmed Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are expecting quarterback J.J. McCarthy to be on their Week 1 roster, general manager Nolan Teasley confirmed Wednesday.

Teasley came short of confirming whether that means McCarthy will back up Kyler Murray, who was named the Vikings' starting quarterback last month.

"J.J. McCarthy's role is to continue to develop, to improve, and to support his teammates, and he's done an excellent job of that," Teasley said.

When asked if McCarthy would serve QB2, Teasley answered, "I wouldn't necessarily comment on depth immediately, but I'm pleased that he's part of our present version of the Minnesota Vikings and excited about his future."

Teasley also said McCarthy has been a full participant in practice for the last two days. ESPN's Kevin Seifert previously reported McCarthy had suffered a "minor ankle injury" in Aug. 22 preseason action.

McCarthy, selected by the Vikings with the No. 10 pick of the 2024 draft, missed the 2024 campaign with a knee injury before leading the Vikings to a 6-4 record in an inconsistent 10 starts last season.

He is the only quarterback on the Vikings roster currently signed through next season, before which both Murray and Carson Wentz are both set to hit unrestricted free agency.

"He's really talented. I think I said that from the jump," Teasley said about McCarthy. "He was picked in the first round for a reason. Really good arm strength, underrated athlete, and looking forward to how he continues to develop in this system.

"I think that the thing you need to keep in mind with J.J. is he has the hardest job in sport. He's only started 10 games, and his story's not written."

McCarthy was splitting second-team reps with Wentz before Sunday's initial roster cutdown, per Seifert .

The Vikings kept four quarterbacks on their roster while cutting down to 53 players and have since signed Max Brosmer to their practice squad.

Teasley said Wednesday he wanted to "keep internal" whether his team had discussed any potential trades involving McCarthy ahead of Sunday's deadline, but noted the Vikings "get calls all the time."

Murray is set to make his first start since his release from the Arizona Cardinals when the Vikings open the regular season Sunday, Sept. 13 against the visiting Green Bay Packers. Teasley and head coach Kevin O'Connell have until then to confirm whether it will be McCarthy or Wentz backing him up.

articles.title: NFL's conduct policy review of Puka Nacua continues and that drives fantasy football managers nuts
articles.summary: Puka Nacua remains under NFL Personal Conduct Policy review amid a civil lawsuit, and discipline could still come even after the Rams' Week 1 opener.
articles.body: Puka Nacua may have NFL wide receiver superpowers, but that doesn't make him invisible to the league's ongoing Personal Conduct Policy review. So the fact he was not suspended over the weekend when the league handed down discipline for three players – placing them on the Commissioner's Exempt List – does not mean Nacua has dodged discipline under the conduct policy. Nacua, perhaps the Los Angeles Rams' most consistent offensive playmaker, is among a group of NFL employees whose situation is still under review after they got into some legal hot water in the offseason. 3 NFL STARS HIT COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST AFTER OFFSEASON FILLED WITH LEGAL TROUBLE That list includes San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York, Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman, Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson and Nacua. All, including Nacua, have off-field issues that have caused the NFL to review their individual situations, with a conduct policy rebuke still possible. And this: The NFL's Week 1 games approaching is not a sign the men in focus will be in the clear once the regular season begins. NFL FACING A DOMESTIC VIOLENCE EPIDEMIC THIS OFFSEASON WITH ARREST OF RAMS LINEMAN THE LATEST CASE The NFL could suspend any of the players or York even after Week 1 if its independent investigations eventually determine that discipline is warranted. There is no firm league deadline requiring a Personal Conduct Policy decision before the season opener. In 2024, for example, then-Buffalo Bills edge rusher Von Miller was suspended on Oct. 1 by the NFL after he had already played multiple games. York is facing league scrutiny tied to his arrest on charges related to a prostitution sting last month. Bateman and Jackson were both arrested on charges related to separate June incidents in separate incidents involving allegations of battery. And Nacua, well, he's the defendant in a civil lawsuit filed by Madison Atiabi, who alleges he bit her shoulder during a New Year's Eve 2025 party. RAMS TROUBLEMAKER WR PUKA NACUA SAYS HE'S A CHANGED MAN AFTER BITING INCIDENT AND STINT IN REHAB Nacua’s attorney denies the allegations and characterizes the biting as "horseplay." (Strange game, if true). Anyway, a Los Angeles County judge has set a civil trial for March 27, 2028. No criminal charges have been filed. The NFL has said nothing publicly beyond the fact that Nacua’s situation remains under league review. Nacua is currently expected to be available for Week 1 but that can change at any time. Well, unlike any of the other players or York, Nacua is a major source of attention in fantasy football because of his prowess in real football. articles.title: Bijan Robinson and Fantasy Football 2026 Safest Players to Draft No. 1
articles.summary: Risk-taking is a must in fantasy football drafts.
articles.body:
Risk-taking is a must in fantasy football drafts.

It's just not something that needs to be done should you be fortunate enough to land the No. 1 pick in your league's draft.

With a selection this early, you're seeking out two things: star potential and safety. It'll be a while until the draft board snakes back your direction, so it's mission-critical for this pick to deliver a difference-maker who's almost guaranteed to produce at an elite level.

And despite the NFL's any-given-Sunday unpredictability, there are a few players who fit this archetype. So, let's minimize risk and maximize the potential return on investment by identifying the three safest players to consider with the No. 1 pick.

There are some theoretical availability concerns tied to Gibbs' lack of size (5'9", 202 lbs), but that's pretty much the extent of any worries tied to making him the first overall pick. And those concerns are seemingly nothing more than theoretical, since he has played all 17 games each of the past two seasons.

As for the safety, well that's tied to a lot of things. His rushing volume is heavy (493 carries the past two seasons), his work as a receiver might be equally spectacular (181 receptions in three seasons) and he has an obvious nose for the end zone (49 career scores in 49 contests).

In fact, his floor probably climbed up a level this offseason upon the exit of David Montgomery, who tallied 33 touchdowns during his three seasons alongside Gibbs. Maybe Gibbs doesn't wind up with all of the goal-line work Montgomery once handled, but even if Gibbs plays a part in Detroit's replacement plan, that could send Gibbs' touchdown count even higher.

If you're holding the No. 1 pick and planning to invest it in Gibbs, you should have a pretty clear idea of baseline expectations. Over the past two seasons, he has landed between 1,800 and 2,000 scrimmage yards with at least 18 touchdowns in each campaign.

When seeking out safety in fantasy football, what you're really looking for is volume. And no one cranks things up quite like Chase, who has led the league in targets each of the past two seasons.

During his five go-rounds in the NFL, he has never seen fewer than the 128 targets he totaled as a rookie in 2021. He's had triple-digit receptions in three consecutive seasons and finished the last two with better than 1,400 receiving yards.

Chase crushes it with both volume and efficiency, and he's almost guaranteed greatness with a healthy Joe Burrow orchestrating this pass-heavy offense. When Burrow stayed upright for all of the 2024 season, Chase delivered true video-game dominance: 127 catches on 175 targets for 1,708 yards and 17 scores—all best-in-the-business marks.

In PPR leagues especially, Chase presents a pretty compelling case for consideration as the first overall pick.

After making Robinson the eighth overall pick of the 2023 draft, the Falcons slowplayed him a bit as a rookie. The kid gloves came off during his sophomore season, though, and those should be buried in the closet by now.

Atlanta tasked him with 365 touches in 2024, and he responded with 1,887 scrimmage yards and 15 touchdowns. He handled one extra touch in 2025 and delivered an NFL-leading 2,298 scrimmage yards with another 11 scores.

A legitimate weapon as both a ball-carrier and a pass-catcher, Robinson is ensured tons of opportunities. His arrow might even be pointed up a bit after the offseason departure of Tyler Allgeier, who dominated the goal-line work and posted 16 touchdowns over the last three seasons.

Folks can argue over whether Robinson has the highest ceiling in fantasy, but his argument for being its safest contributor is a strong one.
